section_map.summary: The six-paragraph summary moves from five aspects and secondary metrics through AHP, FSE, external hit scores, aggregation, extensions, sensitivity, and final communication.
The introduction identifies the Sports Illustrated decision, four required tasks, two prior method families, and a section-by-section route to the deliverables.
The notation binds annual records, AHP quantities, fuzzy and entropy quantities, aggregation weights, and assumptions about omitted factors, data accuracy, and media rankings.
The metric chapter expands five aspects into eighteen secondary indicators and defines wins, losses, SRS, SOS, playoff classes, honors, and contribution scores.
The data section fixes a 75-coach basketball roster, shows coach and season tables, and interpolates missing SRS and SOS from rankings generated by other metrics.
The AHP section builds a three-level hierarchy, pairwise matrix, eigenvector weights, consistency checks, a weighted grade, and a top-ten ranking.
The first FSE stage converts the five aspect definitions into explicit coach-grade formulas for records, game quality, playoffs, honors, and contribution.
The second FSE stage normalizes aspect grades into memberships and derives characteristic shares, entropy, diversity, criterion weights, and a final grade.
The evaluation section compares AHP and FSE with media-ranking offset distances and a hit score while exposing the benchmark dependence.
The aggregation section weights AHP and FSE inversely by their offset distances and reports the combined rank and hit scores.
The gender extension reruns the model on a women-basketball roster and compares its top ten with a Yahoo list.
The time extension divides NCAA history into six periods, assigns judgmental time weights, rebuilds annual metrics, and compares three changed rankings and hit scores.
The cross-sport extension maps basketball playoff and honor fields to football and ice hockey, adjusts metrics and rules, applies time weights, and reports new lists.
The first sensitivity study compares three membership-function families, traces entropy-weight changes over k, and chooses a hit-score maximizing configuration.
The second sensitivity study varies the win-to-loss weight ratio and selects the ratio two using the same media hit-score benchmark.
The third sensitivity study varies the AHP share, tracks rank changes, and selects an AHP weight near 0.1 to 0.2 by hit score.
The exploration remaps five evaluation aspects to 43 U.S. presidents and reports a top-ten list as a transfer demonstration.
The closing assessment preserves the model's breadth, explicit metrics, and adjustment workflow before stating data, subjectivity, and reproducibility limits.
The final ranked table and nontechnical explanation translate the model route into lists and a sports-fan-facing account of scores and relative position.
The future-work paragraph asks for broader data and improved quantification, while the references identify sources without freezing the data or code.

assumptions.summary: The five retained aspects and eighteen secondary indicators are assumed to play a vital role in coach evaluation.
Ignored coach attributes are assumed not to change the ranking.
Collected and interpolated data are assumed sufficient, accurate, and correctly quantified.
Selected media rankings are assumed to reflect an objective and accurate ranking to some extent.
One-nine pairwise judgments and the resulting eigenvectors are assumed to encode criterion importance.
Each aspect is treated as benefit-oriented and normalized by its observed maximum.
Absolute media-rank offsets are assumed comparable across lists with potentially different methods and rosters.
Six historical periods and their assigned weights are assumed to represent changes in coaching opportunity.
Football and ice-hockey stages, awards, and time effects are assumed mappable to the basketball interface.
Presidential qualities are assumed sufficiently analogous to the five coach aspects for exploratory transfer.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The basketball roster contains 70 Hall of Fame coaches plus five additional contributors selected by the authors.
Coach metrics are collected from sports-reference.com, Wikipedia, NCAA material, and other Internet sources without frozen snapshots.
Table 3.1 shows ten of 75 candidate records with career years, wins, losses, SRS, SOS, and playoff outcomes.
Table 3.2 exposes Larry Brown's annual record as an example of the season-level input used by the time extension.
Missing SRS and SOS values are interpolated according to rankings generated by other metrics, creating a model-dependent imputation.
AHP uses a five-by-five criteria matrix and secondary-level vectors, including the printed historical-record vector [1.5, -0.5].
Table 4.3 reports ten coaches' characteristic values, diversity factors, entropy weights, and FSE grades.
External top-ten lists are attributed to ESPN, Bleacher Report, Yahoo Sports, and Sporting News but are not archived.
The women-basketball application uses one collected roster and one Yahoo ranking comparator.
Historical turning points define six periods whose weights are selected by the authors.
Cross-sport tables map basketball playoff rounds and honor fields to football bowls and ice-hockey stages.
The president exploration uses 43 presidents and multiple poll sources without publishing a frozen feature table or calculation file.

models.summary: Define five aspects and eighteen secondary indicators as typed inputs for both coach-ranking models.
Derive criterion and alternative weights, check consistency, and calculate the AHP ranking grade.
Convert the five aspect definitions into a coach-specific grade vector for FSE.
Normalize five benefit-oriented aspect grades into the fuzzy matrix.
Derive criterion shares, entropy, diversity, weights, and the FSE grade.
Compare AHP and FSE ranks with selected media lists through absolute offsets and hit scores.
Combine AHP and FSE grades with offset-linked weights and produce the final rank.
Rerun the coach-ranking interface for a women-basketball roster and compare it with one media list.
Apply judgmental six-period weights to annual metrics and compare AHP, FSE, and AM ranks before and after weighting.
Map basketball fields to football and ice-hockey metrics, adjust rules and time weights, and report sport-specific lists.
Sweep membership families, exponent k, win-to-loss ratio, and aggregation weight while tracing hit score and rank response.
Remap the five-aspect interface to presidents and translate the coach model into a sports-fan-facing explanation.

dependency_graph.handoff: The five aspects and secondary factors enter the AHP hierarchy and weighted grade.
The same typed metrics are transformed into the five FSE aspect grades.
The five aspect grades are normalized coach-by-coach into memberships.
The fuzzy matrix supplies characteristic shares for entropy weighting and the FSE grade.
The AHP top-ten list enters the external offset and hit-score comparison.
The FSE top-ten list enters the same declared comparison.
Component distances determine aggregation weights, while component grades determine the combined score.
The complete ranking interface is rerun on the women-basketball roster.
The base interface receives six-period weighted annual metrics for before-and-after comparison.
The historical weighting idea and model interface are adapted after sport-specific metric mapping.
FSE memberships and entropy weights are recomputed across alternative function families and k values.
The aggregation grade is rerun across AHP weights while hit score and rank changes are traced.
The transfer workflow motivates the president exploration, and qualified coach lists feed the nontechnical explanation.

verification.summary: The AHP criteria matrix reports CI=0.301 and CR=0.0269 and states that all secondary vectors satisfy CR<0.1.
verification.strength: The source gives the intended gate before accepting weights.
verification.limitation: Judgment provenance and recomputation files are absent.

verification.summary: Table 4.2 exposes AHP grades and ranks for ten basketball coaches.
verification.strength: Names, scores, and order are visible.
verification.limitation: Only a sample roster and no executable calculation are frozen.

verification.summary: Table 4.3 exposes FSE inputs, entropy-derived values, and grades.
verification.strength: The intended entropy-to-grade route is inspectable.
verification.limitation: A duplicate X3 header and truncated coach name require reconciliation.

verification.summary: Top-five, six-to-ten, and overall distances and hit scores are reported separately for AHP and FSE.
verification.limitation: All benchmark lists are treated as accurate without independent validation.

verification.summary: Table 5.2 compares AHP, FSE, and AM ranks and hit scores.
verification.strength: The aggregate is compared against both components.
verification.limitation: The same media lists both set aggregation weights and score the result.

verification.summary: The gender application compares the women-coach rank with one Yahoo list.
verification.strength: The interface is shown on a different roster.
verification.limitation: One sport, roster, and comparator cannot establish a general gender conclusion.

verification.summary: Time-weighted equations reconstruct annual record, rating, and playoff inputs.
verification.strength: The declared historical mechanism is explicit.
verification.limitation: The period weights are judgmental and SRS/SOS symbols are misdescribed as losses.

verification.summary: Before-and-after AHP, FSE, and AM tables show score and order changes under time weights.
verification.strength: Rank movement is visible for all three models.
verification.limitation: The chosen media hit score declines after the extension.

verification.summary: A four-step flow chart states adjust metrics, calculation rules, time weights, then solve.
verification.strength: The cross-sport interface is compact and reproducible in concept.
verification.limitation: No independent receiving-sport validation is reported.

verification.summary: Membership-family hit-score curves compare three functions over k.
verification.strength: Function and parameter response are visible.
verification.limitation: The same benchmark used to design the model selects the preferred function.

verification.summary: The win-to-loss ratio curve identifies a local hit-score maximum near two.
verification.limitation: No uncertainty or alternate benchmark is used.

verification.summary: Aggregation-weight curves trace rank changes and hit score over the AHP share.
verification.strength: Score and ranking effects are both considered.
verification.limitation: The selected 0.1-0.2 range is optimized on the same comparison lists.

verification.summary: The president list demonstrates a remapped domain output.
verification.strength: A distinct domain is processed through a comparable five-aspect structure.
verification.limitation: Metric construction and independent validation are not supplied.

verification.summary: The final coach table and nontechnical explanation reconnect outputs to the five-aspect model.
verification.strength: The audience artifact remains connected to the method.
verification.limitation: Frozen data, code, and full reproducibility evidence are absent.

results_trace.summary: AHP ranks Mike Krzyzewski first and John Wooden second, with playoff performance receiving the largest criteria weight.
FSE ranks John Wooden first at 0.8708 and Mike Krzyzewski second at 0.8629, with near-equal aspect weights.
FSE's reported overall hit score is 81.81 compared with AHP's 78.77.
AM ranks John Wooden, Mike Krzyzewski, Adolph Rupp, Dean Smith, and Bob Knight as its basketball top five.
AM's reported top-five, top-ten, and overall hit scores exceed the corresponding AHP and FSE values in Table 5.2.
The women-basketball rerun reports a top ten and uses overlap with Yahoo to claim gender does not matter.
Time weights change multiple AHP and FSE grades and positions.
Time weighting changes AM's first two places and lowers the selected benchmark hit score.
The narrative says earlier coaches tend to fall and modern coaches tend to rise under the chosen period weights.
Cross-sport application reports Bear Bryant first in football and Bob Johnson first in ice hockey.
Membership family 1 at k=3 is selected as the preferred FSE configuration by hit score.
The win-to-loss weight ratio two is selected as the preferred historical-record rule.
The aggregation hit score is reported maximal for an AHP share near 0.1 to 0.2.
The president exploration ranks Abraham Lincoln, George Washington, and Franklin D. Roosevelt as its top three.
The final table publishes top-five basketball, football, and ice-hockey coach lists.

contributions.summary: A five-aspect, eighteen-indicator hierarchy gives both component models a shared typed interface.
AHP exposes hierarchy, pairwise comparison, normalized eigenvector, consistency, and grade steps.
FSE combines source-defined aspect grades with membership normalization and entropy-derived weights.
Offset distances and hit scores make the chosen external comparison explicit rather than implicit.
The aggregation layer separates component grades from the rule that weights them.
The time extension reconstructs annual metrics rather than adding a detached bonus to the final score.
A four-step cross-sport workflow states which interfaces must change before transfer.
Three sensitivity studies expose membership, calculation, and aggregation choices.
The final three-sport table and nontechnical explanation form a visible model-to-audience handoff.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary previews the complete metric-to-model-to-check-to-extension route, but award status alone does not prove why judges valued it.
The three-model comparison makes the aggregation choice visible, without proving benchmark independence.
The three-sport table and nontechnical explanation produce an audience-ready artifact, without proving universal ranking truth.

weaknesses.summary: Table 4.3 prints X1, X2, X3, X3, X5, Y2, so the fourth aspect header must be reconciled before machine reuse.
Table 4.3 genuinely truncates Mike Krzyzewski to Mike Krzy; the source label must not be silently completed inside the frozen transcription.
The descriptions below equation 6.1 incorrectly call SRS_i and SOS_i losses per year rather than rating and schedule-strength values.
The historical-record alternative vector [1.5, -0.5] mixes a negative loss coefficient into an AHP-weight display and needs explicit interpretation and unit handling.
Selected media rankings are treated as an objective accurate standard without independent validation, frozen lists, or roster reconciliation.
The gender conclusion rests on one women-basketball roster and a media hit score and cannot support a general cross-gender claim.
Six period weights are judgmental, and the resulting extension reduces the chosen media hit score rather than independently improving validity.
Cross-sport transfer is demonstrated through adapted metrics and lists but not through independent football or hockey validation.
Membership, win-loss, and aggregation settings are selected using the same hit-score benchmark already used to evaluate the models.
Formula, table, ranking, sensitivity, and transfer claims lack frozen input data, executable code, environment metadata, and complete reproducibility artifacts.

independent_extensions.summary: Archive the complete 75-coach roster, annual records, missingness map, retrieval dates, and interpolation code.
Reconstruct each AHP matrix from documented judgments and reconcile the negative historical-record coefficient.
Repair Table 4.3's fourth criterion header and coach identifier through a versioned correction record.
Freeze every external ranking list and evaluate against held-out or expert-designed criteria rather than the same fit target.
Test gender claims with matched multi-sport cohorts, uncertainty intervals, and explicit measurement invariance.
Estimate or scenario-test time weights and correct SRS/SOS symbol descriptions before reranking.
Validate football and hockey mappings against sport-specific held-out outcomes and expert review.
Separate model selection from evaluation by using nested or held-out benchmark lists for sensitivity choices.
Publish executable calculations, schemas, environment locks, intermediate tables, integrity checks, and uncertainty reports.
